title: Week 8 Assessment: Integration
intro: This assessment integrates careers, conflict, presenting and networking with everything before it. Part A is auto-graded from lessons you completed. Part B has a decision scenario, an interview role-play and a written task. Combine skills as you would in a real workplace.

concepts.label: Career Planning and Personal Branding: applied

items.prompt: You reach an interview 20 minutes early. The receptionist asks you to wait, and the interviewer is delayed by 30 minutes. What is the best behaviour?

options.feedback: Complaining creates a poor first impression.

options.text: Wait calmly, review your notes, keep your phone silent and greet people politely.
options.feedback: Patience and courtesy are part of professionalism.

options.text: Leave and send an angry message.
options.feedback: Leaving without discussion damages your chances.

items.why: Everyone you meet may influence the decision, so stay patient and polite.

items.setup: You are in an interview for an entry-level SAP ABAP role. The panel will ask about your preparation, a failure and a conflict at work.

turns.they: Tell us about a time you failed and what you learned.

options.text: I failed a mock technical test because I had not practised under time limits. I did a post-mortem, took three timed practice sets and improved from 40 to 70 per cent.
options.feedback: A specific story with analysis and results.

turns.they: How do you handle disagreement in a team?

options.text: I avoid people I disagree with.
I clarify what matters to each of us, offer options and agree on a specific next step, in writing if needed.
I just do what the loudest person says.
options.feedback: Passive compliance is not a strategy.

turns.they: Do you have any questions for us?

options.feedback: A good candidate usually asks something.

options.text: What would the first 90 days look like for a trainee, and how is learning supported?
options.feedback: A thoughtful question that shows planning.

options.text: How soon can I get a raise?
options.feedback: This focuses on pay before contribution.

items.why: Use specific stories, constructive conflict habits and thoughtful questions in interviews.

items.prompt: Write 100 to 130 words: a follow-up message to a senior professional you met last week that thanks them, reminds them of your conversation, makes one specific small request and offers something useful in return.

descriptors.3: Real offer with a warm, professional tone.

items.modelAnswer: Dear Ms Rao, thank you for the time you gave me at the campus event last Thursday. Your point about writing clean ABAP and testing small programs stayed with me. I have started a weekly mini-program habit based on it. If you are open to it, could I send you a short summary of my practice projects and ask for two lines of feedback? I would be happy to share the notes I made from the session with other students in return. Thank you again. Regards, Deepak.
items.guidance: Strong messages are short, specific about the earlier conversation, make a small clear ask and offer something in return. Avoid asking for a job directly in the first message.
